readings.title: Peace, Prudence, and Strife
readings.subtitle: A collection of proverbs contrasting wise and foolish behavior in matters of wealth, family, and conflict.
readings.text: [Proverbs 17:1] Better is a dry piece of bread and rest with it, Than a house filled with slaughters of strife. [2] A wise servant rules over a son who causes shame, And shares an inheritance among the brothers. [3] A refining pot is for silver and a furnace for gold, But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> tries <dn>את</dn> the hearts. [4] An evil-doer gives heed to wicked lips; A liar gives ear to a tongue of desire. [5] He who mocks the poor reproaches <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> Maker; He who rejoices at calamity does not go unpunished. [6] Children’s children are the crown of old men, And the adornment of children is their fathers. [7] Excellent speech is not fitting for a fool, Much less lying lips for a noble. [8] A bribe is a stone of favour in the eyes of its owner; Wherever he turns, he prospers. [9] He who covers <dn>את</dn> a transgression seeks <dn>את</dn> love, But he who repeats a matter separates intimate friends. [10] Reproof enters deeper into a wise man Than a hundred strikes on a fool. [11] An evil one seeks only <dn>את</dn> rebellion, So a cruel messenger is sent against him. [12] Let a bereaved bear meet a man, Rather than a fool in his folly. [13] Whoever rewards <dn>את</dn> evil for good, Evil does not leave his house. [14] The beginning of strife is like releasing water; Therefore stop <dn>את</dn> fighting before it breaks out.

readings.title: Justice, Friendship, and Speech
readings.subtitle: Proverbs concerning right-ruling, the nature of true friendship, and the power of words.
readings.text: [15] He who declares <dn>את</dn> the wrong right, And he who condemns <dn>את</dn> the righteous, Both of them are an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [16] Why is this – a price in the hand Of a fool to buy <dn>את</dn> wisdom, When there is no heart? [17] A friend loves at all times, And a brother is born for adversity. [18] A man lacking heart shakes hands in a pledge, He becomes a guarantor for his friend. [19] He who loves <dn>את</dn> transgression loves <dn>את</dn> strife, He who exalts his door seeks <dn>את</dn> destruction. [20] He who has a crooked heart finds <dn>את</dn> no good, And he who has a perverse tongue falls into evil. [21] He who brings forth a fool has sorrow for it, And the father of a fool has no joy. [22] A rejoicing heart causes good healing, But a stricken spirit dries <dn>את</dn> the bones. [23] One who is wrong accepts <dn>את</dn> a bribe behind the back To pervert <dn>את</dn> the paths of right-ruling. [24] Wisdom is before the face of the understanding one, But the eyes of a fool are on the ends of the earth. [25] A foolish son is a grief to his father, And bitterness to her who bore him. [26] It is also not good to punish <dn>את</dn> the righteous one, To strike <dn>את</dn> noble ones for straightness. [27] He who has knowledge spares <dn>את</dn> his words, And a man of understanding is cool of spirit. [28] Even a fool keeping silence is regarded as wise, As understanding, when he closes <dn>את</dn> his lips.

readings.title: The Fool's Folly and the Lord's Fortress
readings.subtitle: Wisdom on understanding, strife, slander, and the security found in the Name of YeHoVaH.
readings.text: [Proverbs 18:1] The separatist seeks <dn>את</dn> his own desire; He breaks out against all sound wisdom. [2] A fool does not delight in understanding, But in uncovering <dn>את</dn> his own heart. [3] When a wrong one comes, scorn comes too. And with shame comes reproach. [4] The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters; The fountain of wisdom is a flowing stream. [5] It is not good to show partiality to the wrong, Or to turn aside <dn>את</dn> the righteous in right-ruling. [6] A fool’s lips enter into strife, And his mouth calls for blows. [7] A fool’s mouth is his ruin, And his lips are the snare of his life. [8] The words of a slanderer are like delicacies, And they go down into the inner parts of the heart. [9] Also, he who is slack in his work Is a brother of a master destroyer. [10] The Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a strong tower; The righteous run into it and are safe. [11] The rich man’s wealth is his strong city, And like a high wall in his own imagination. [12] Before destruction the heart of a man is haughty, And before esteem is humility.

readings.title: The Power of the Tongue
readings.subtitle: Proverbs on listening before speaking, the strength of the human spirit, and the life-and-death power of words.
readings.text: [13] He who answers <dn>את</dn> a matter before he hears <dn>את</dn> it, It is folly and shame to him. [14] The spirit of a man sustains him in sickness, But who does bear <dn>את</dn> a broken spirit? [15] The heart of the understanding one gets <dn>את</dn> knowledge, And the ear of the wise seeks <dn>את</dn> knowledge. [16] A man’s gift makes room for him, And brings him before great men. [17] The first to state his own case, seems right, Until another comes and examines him. [18] The lot settles <dn>את</dn> disputes, And separates between the mighty. [19] A brother transgressed against is a strong city, And contentions are like the bars of a citadel. [20] A man’s stomach is satisfied From the fruit of his mouth; He is satisfied with the increase of his lips. [21] Death and life are in the power of the tongue, And those loving it eat <dn>את</dn> its fruit. [22] He who has found <dn>את</dn> a wife has found <dn>את</dn> good, And receives favour from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] The poor speaks beseechingly, But the rich answers fiercely. [24] A man of many friends might come to ruin, But there is a Loving One Who sticks closer than a brother!

readings.title: Integrity Over Wealth
readings.subtitle: Contrasts between the poor but righteous and the wealthy but foolish, with warnings against false witness.
readings.text: [Proverbs 19:1] Better is the poor walking in his integrity Than one of perverse lips, who is a fool. [2] Also, desire without knowledge is not good; And he who hurries with his feet sins. [3] The foolishness of a man perverts <dn>את</dn> his way, And <dn>his</dn> heart is wroth against <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] Wealth adds many friends, But the poor is separated from his friend. [5] A false witness does not go unpunished, And he who breaths out lies does not escape. [6] Many entreat <dn>את</dn> the favour of the noble. And all are friends to him who gives gifts. [7] All the brothers of the poor shall hate him; How much more shall his friends go far from him! He pursues <dn>את</dn> promises – they are gone!. [8] He who gets <dn>את</dn> heart loves <dn>את</dn> his own life; He who guards <dn>את</dn> understanding finds good. [9] A false witness does not go unpunished, And he who breathes out lies perishes. [10] Luxury is not fitting for a fool, Much less for a servant to rule over princes. [11] A man’s discretion makes him patient, And his adorning is to pass over <dn>את</dn> a transgression. [12] The sovereign’s wrath is like the roaring of a lion, But his delight is like dew on the grass.

readings.title: The Household and the Heart
readings.subtitle: Wisdom concerning family strife, laziness, the importance of discipline, and the sovereignty of YeHoVaH's plans.
readings.text: [13] A foolish son is a calamity to his father, And the contentions of a wife are a continual dripping. [14] Houses and riches are the inheritance from fathers, But an understanding wife is from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [15] Laziness makes one fall into a deep sleep, And an idle being suffers hunger. [16] He who guards <dn>את</dn> the command guards <dn>את</dn> his life, <dn>He</dn> who despises <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> ways dies. [17] He who shows favour to the poor lends to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, And <dn>He</dn> repays <dn>את</dn> his deed. [18] Discipline <dn>את</dn> your son because there is expectation, And do not set <dn>את</dn> your being on his destruction. [19] One of great wrath bears <dn>את</dn> punishment; For if you rescue him, You only have to do it again. [20] Listen to <dn>את</dn> counsel and accept <dn>את</dn> discipline, So that you are wise in your latter end. [21] Many are the plans in a man’s heart, But it is the counsel of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that stands.

readings.title: The Certainty of Judgment
readings.subtitle: Final proverbs in this chapter on character, laziness, the value of reproof, and the fate of scoffers and fools.
readings.text: [22] What is desirable in a man is his loving-commitment, And a poor man is better than a liar. [23] The fear of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> leads to life, And he remains satisfied, He is not visited by evil. [24] A lazy one buries <dn>את</dn> his hand in a dish, And does not bring <dn>את</dn> it back to his mouth. [25] Strike <dn>את</dn> a scoffer, and the simple is made wise; And reprove <dn>את</dn> one who has understanding, And he discerns <dn>את</dn> knowledge. [26] He who plunders <dn>את</dn> a father, Chases away <dn>את</dn> his mother, Is a son causing shame and bringing reproach. [27] Cease, my son, to hear <dn>את</dn> discipline, And you shall stray from the words of knowledge. [28] A witness of Beliya‛al scorns <dn>את</dn> right-ruling, And the mouth of the wrong ones Devours <dn>את</dn> wickedness. [29] Judgments are in store for scoffers, And beatings for the backs of fools.
